top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
top_sast_rules.description: Reinterpreting text from the DOM as HTML can lead to a cross-site scripting vulnerability.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Detect output operations that lack proper encoding for the target context
top_sast_rules.remediation: Use context-appropriate encoding for all output operations. Implement proper escaping for HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and URL contexts.

top_sast_rules.description: DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-676. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
top_sast_rules.description: File access follows a symlink, hardlink, or shortcut to an unintended resource.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-59 symlink hardlink link-following symbolic-link file-link archive-extraction path-resolution file-overwrite race filesystem
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject unsafe links and verify resolved file targets before access.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')
top_sast_rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with arbitrary internal entity expansion is vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement resource consumption limits, rate limiting, and proper cleanup mechanisms for all operations.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
top_sast_rules.description: Modifying an object obtained via a user-controlled property name may lead to accidental mutation of the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement proper output encoding based on context (HTML, JavaScript, CSS, URL). Use Content Security Policy and validate input.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
top_sast_rules.description: A 'for' loop that increments its loop variable but checks it against a lower bound, or decrements its loop variable but checks it against an upper bound, will either stop iterating immediately or keep iterating indefinitely, and is usually indicative of a typo.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement loop bounds and timeout mechanisms. Add maximum iteration counts. Use break conditions that cannot be controlled by user input.

top_sast_rules.description: A security-relevant comparison checks the wrong, incomplete, or non-canonical value.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-697 incorrect-comparison equality compare comparator mismatch canonicalization hostname url signature token partial-comparison substring
top_sast_rules.remediation: Compare canonical complete values with the intended security predicate.

top_sast_rules.description: Matching a URL or hostname against a regular expression that contains an unescaped dot as part of the hostname might match more hostnames than expected.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement strict input validation using allowlists and reject invalid input rather than attempting to sanitize it.
